title: Urban Company Raises ₹2,500 Cr Via QIP, Draws Bids Worth Over ₹15,000 Cr
summary: Urban Company raises 2500 crore rupees through qualified institutional placement
detailed: Urban Company raised ₹2,500 Cr through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), drawing bids worth over ₹15,000 Cr from more than 60 institutional investors.
Key allocations include ₹600 Cr for the InstaHelp service professional ecosystem, ₹540 Cr for marketing, and ₹200 Cr for technology development, with shares allocated at ₹156 apiece.
Involved participants include over 60 domestic and global institutional investors, with mutual funds securing over 50% of the allocation.
This capital injection supports long-term expansion and scaling of services despite the company's consolidated net loss widening to ₹182.5 Cr in Q2 FY27.
sentences: Urban Company has raised ₹2,500 Cr through a QIP, attracting bids worth over ₹15,000 Cr from more than 60 domestic and global institutional investors.
The company plans to deploy ₹600 Cr towards InstaHelp’s service professional ecosystem, alongside investments in technology, marketing, and its Native products business.

Home services marketplace Urban Company has raised ₹2,500 Cr through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), attracting bids worth over ₹15,000 Cr, more than 6X the issue size.
The issue opened on November 16 (Monday) and closed yesterday.
More than 60 investors submitted bids, with shares allocated to 33 investors.
Of these, 13 did not hold Urban Company shares before the issue.

Mutual funds accounted for more than 50% of the allocation, including SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Mirae Asset Mutual Fund, Invesco Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Kotak Mutual Fund and Nippon India Mutual Fund, among others.
Domestic insurers HDFC Life, Bajaj Life Insurance, and Edelweiss Life also participated.
Global institutional investors included Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Norges Bank Investment Management, Amundi, Pictet, and Manulife, while Premji Invest was among the domestic investors.
Consequently, Urban Company’s Fund Raise Committee approved the allotment of 16.02 Cr equity shares at an issue price of ₹156 apiece, marking a 3.1% discount to the floor price of ₹161.03 per share.
The company had said earlier that it may offer a discount of up to 5% to the floor price for the QIP.
Urban Company outlined the fundraise plan last month to invest across its businesses, strengthen InstaHelp’s market position, and pursue acquisitions.
According to its preliminary placement document, the company plans to deploy ₹600 Cr towards expanding InstaHelp’s service professional ecosystem.
This includes minimum earnings guarantees, referral payouts, and training and onboarding costs.
The allocation comprises ₹150 Cr in FY27, ₹300 Cr in FY28, and ₹150 Cr in FY29.
InstaHelp allows households to book service professionals for tasks such as cleaning, mopping, laundry, and basic meal preparation.
The company plans to build service professional availability ahead of demand when entering new neighbourhoods.

Urban Company has earmarked another ₹540 Cr for marketing, ₹200 Cr for technology development and cloud infrastructure, ₹85 Cr for lease rentals for offices and training centres, and ₹50 Cr for research and development for Native products.
A portion of the proceeds will also fund potential acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
Native, Urban Company’s home products business, currently sells water purifiers and smart locks.
Yesterday, the company’s board approved adding residential air conditioners to the portfolio, following in-principle approval to explore the category last month.
The fundraise follows a widening of Urban Company’s consolidated net loss to ₹182.5 Cr in Q2 FY27, more than tripling from ₹59.3 Cr a year earlier.
Operating revenue rose 41.4% to ₹537.3 Cr from ₹380 Cr, while total expenses increased 61.5% to ₹745.7 Cr.
The fresh capital will support further expansion while Urban Company builds demand and service professional availability.
Management has set FY31 as InstaHelp’s breakeven target, indicating a prolonged investment period for the business.
Shares of Urban Company were trading 3.81% lower at ₹169.05 on the BSE at 09:50 IST.
